transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I’m having a hard time keeping things organized. There are a lot of moving parts—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I keep ending up doing whatever feels most urgent or loud, not necessarily what actually matters. It’s been getting harder to manage.
Did you have similar problems with organization and getting pulled to whatever felt most urgent when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. Looking back, it was there in grade school. Teachers would say I was bright, but I daydreamed a lot. I’d forget to turn in work even when it was finished, and I was always losing homework folders. That was before I was a teenager.
Do you often make careless mistakes because your attention drifts, even when a task is important to you?

Yeah. In code reviews especially, I’ll miss something really small… like a condition that’s flipped the wrong way, or a version number in a dependency file. Then later I look at it and it was right there. I just skimmed past it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work over and over because you’re worried you might have missed something?
I don’t know that I’d say over and over. I’ll check things, sure, but… I’m not sure it’s in that worried kind of way you mean.
Have you ever had a period of several days when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?
Not that I can think of. I mean, I’ve had busy stretches where I stayed up late, but not… several days where I felt unusually energized and didn’t need sleep.
Do you often put off tasks that require sustained mental effort, like paperwork or detailed reading?
Maybe. I mean, paperwork and long reading aren’t my favorite, so I’ll sometimes push them off, but I’m not sure it’s more than most people do.
Do these organization and attention problems also cause trouble for you in your daily life outside of work?

Outside of work… I guess I notice it less there. The bigger problem has been at work, honestly. It’s started to affect how people see me — I missed a patent filing checkpoint, and after a rough architecture review, some collaborators seemed to be questioning whether I should be leading the bigger project.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about work stuff sometimes, but not… lots of different things all the time, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you often get so focused on making something perfect that it takes much longer to finish than it should?
I’m not sure. I can get picky about things sometimes, but I don’t think it’s usually about making it perfect. At least, I haven’t really noticed that as the main reason things take longer.
